standard.title: Read accurately and fluently
standard.description: read a range of texts using phonic, semantic and grammatical knowledge to read accurately and fluently, and monitor and self-correct
standard.prior_knowledge: Students read with phrasing and fluency, monitoring meaning by re-reading and self-correcting (AC9E2LY04). They have not yet applied all three knowledge types — phonic, semantic and grammatical — explicitly as coordinated reading tools across a wider range of texts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students read a range of texts using phonic, semantic and grammatical knowledge to read accurately and fluently, monitoring and self-correcting.

nodes.label: Using multiple knowledge sources to decode
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use phonic, vocabulary and grammatical knowledge together to read unknown words accurately.
nodes.minimum_width: When encountering an unknown word, apply at least two knowledge sources (e.g. phonic knowledge + sentence grammar) and explain the decoding process.
nodes.typical_width: Use phonic knowledge, word knowledge, vocabulary and grammatical knowledge to read unknown words; read a wider range of texts from different learning areas including chapter books.
wider: Compare how you approach an unknown proper noun versus an unknown content word — discussing how different knowledge sources are more or less useful for each
Reflect on decoding strategies used across subject-area texts and identify which strategy is most useful for technical vocabulary
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who have not consolidated multi-source decoding cannot fluently monitor for meaning at N2 — monitoring requires decoding to be sufficiently automated that attention is freed for comprehension.

response_modes.reason: Fluent multi-source decoding develops through reading practice across a wide range of text types. Strategy knowledge is not the bottleneck — application under real reading conditions is.

success_criteria: Student attempts to read unknown words using multiple sources (not just phonics alone or skipping)
Student self-corrects when an initial reading doesn't make sense

nodes.label: Monitoring and self-correcting
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can monitor their own reading for meaning and self-correct errors that disrupt comprehension.
nodes.minimum_width: Demonstrate monitoring by identifying at least one point in a read text where meaning was disrupted, and explain what was done to repair it.
nodes.typical_width: Monitor meaning during reading and self-correct — re-reading, trying alternative decodings, using context — to maintain fluent and accurate reading across chapter books and curriculum texts.
wider: Discuss which self-correction strategies work best for different types of errors (unknown word vs wrong word that sounds similar)
Observe and compare the monitoring strategies of a proficient and a developing reader, discussing what makes the proficient reader effective
success_criteria: Student notices when their reading doesn't make sense and stops to self-correct
Student applies at least one repair strategy (re-read, try alternative, use context) rather than continuing past the error
